ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against TRACFIN dissuasion files, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, OFAC SDN list (where applicable to USD transactions), and United Nations Security Council terrorism financing lists. PEP identification is required under Article L. 561-10-2 CMF; enhanced due diligence is triggered for politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates; systematic adverse-media and corporate-ownership-piercing review is mandatory before engagement with any UBO. For this high-risk supplement e-commerce activity, source-of-funds verification is required for all non-EU UBOs.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des formalités d'entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; operated by INPI); RCS database consultations via infogreffe.fr.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed company name must be expressed in the Latin alphabet. Where a non-Latin-script language (e.g., Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic) is used, a single Latin-script transliteration must be adopted and written into the articles of incorporation; the transliteration must be free of characters that impair registry search. French law (loi n° 94-665 du 4 août 1994) does not prohibit foreign-language names, but prohibits misleading terms and requires the corporate-form marker 'SAS' to be presented accurately.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Crédit / Société de financement — requires ACPR banking authorization
Assurance / Mutuelle / Caisse de retraite — requires insurance-code approval
Pharmacie / Officine / Drugstore — restricted by Public Health Code and pharmacist licensing
France / République / État / National — may mislead as to public or sovereign character
Chambre de commerce / Barreau / Avocat — reserved to regulated professional bodies

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the INPI/Guichet Unique refuses a proposed name, the applicant receives a written decision stating whether the refusal is based on identity/confusion with an existing legal entity or on public-policy grounds. Within two months of refusal, the applicant may file a recours gracieux with the Director of INPI. If that is refused, a formal administrative appeal may be brought before the Tribunal administratif de Paris within two months under Articles R. 421-1 to R. 421-5 of the Code de justice administrative. Where the dispute concerns trademark or name confusion, the applicant may also petition the President of the Tribunal judiciaire in emergency summary proceedings (référé). In parallel, the applicant may obtain the written consent of the conflicting prior owner and resubmit the amended name. Fees are non-refundable and a new filing is required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Under Articles L. 123-11-1 and R. 123-139 of the French Code de commerce, the registered office of an SAS may be domiciled with a prefecture-approved commercial domiciliation provider, provided a formal domiciliation contract is concluded and the provider's authorization is in place. A mere P.O. box or virtual mailbox is insufficient. For a France-based e-commerce retail activity, a virtual office satisfies initial RCS registration, but the fiscal and customs authorities (DGFiP and Douanes) may require demonstrable commercial substance — physical storage, logistics, or local management — before recognising French siness continuity and VAT input credits or granting an EORI number free of scrutiny.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high. Estimated 35% likelihood of an unannounced DGCCRF or registral on-site control within the first 24 months, because retail dietary supplements are a priority inspection sector in France. DGFiP audit probability for a newly formed SAS in the e-commerce sector is approximately 12-15% per annum. The high-risk AML classification increases the probability of UBO-register compliance visits by the registry authority.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce) — general company formation provisions at Articles L. 210-1 to L. 210-10 and SAS-specific provisions at Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-30; registration and RCS formalities at Articles R. 210-1 et seq. and R. 227-1 et seq. (Decree No. 67-236 of 23 March 1967 as amended); Article 1835 of the Civil Code for corporate object; applicable INPI GEF filing instructions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) kept by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the jurisdiction of the registered office, with electronic intake through the national single portal INPI Guichet Électronique des Formalités des Entreprises (GEF) — formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Demande d'immatriculation d'une personne morale (Form M0 / Cerfa 3220), together with the executed Statuts (Articles of Association) and supporting exhibits, filed electronically via the GEF; completion evidenced by the Kbis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies to an SAS (Article L. 227-2 of the Code de commerce); the share capital is freely fixed in the Statuts. Cash subscriptions must be deposited into a blocked escrow account held with a French credit institution, the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or a notary until the RCS registration; in-kind contributions must be fully paid up at incorporation. Recommended paid-up capital for this project: EUR 1,000.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, THAT the share capital of the company, as set out in the Statuts, has been fully subscribed. Each subscriber irrevocably commits to pay the subscribed cash contributions into a blocked account held with a French credit institution or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, such funds to remain escrowed until registration of the company.

RESOLVED FURTHER, THAT the registered office is hereby established at the address stated in the Statuts and remains effective from the date of registration in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés.

RESOLVED FINALLY, THAT the President and, where applicable, the Directeur Général be and are hereby appointed with the powers and terms set out in the Statuts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Statuts and Full Share Subscription (Founding Act)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders acting by private deed (sous seing privé) or by notarial act if real property is contributed; no governmental pre-clearance required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding shareholders sign the Statuts and subscribe the whole of the share capital. The Statuts must state the legal form (SAS), corporate name, registered office, corporate object covering cross-border e-commerce of dietary supplements (ISIC 4791), duration (99 years), share capital, classes and terms of shares, governance bodies and powers of the President. The founders complete the beneficial-owner declaration (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs, Article L. 561-46 of the Monetary and Financial Code) and verify the President's legal capacity and absence of disqualification.
required_dossiers: Final draft Statuts conforming to Decree No. 67-236 of 23 March 1967 (Annexe I)
Identity document and proof of address of each shareholder
Attestation of non-conviction / corporate capacity for the designated President
Kbis or equivalent extract for any corporate shareholder
Contribution-in-kind appraisal report with appraiser's valuation, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deed is refused or queried by a notary or registry, amend the defective clauses (object, capital or governance provisions) and re-execute the Statuts; if the corporate object conflicts with regulated supplement rules, narrow it to lawful e-commerce distribution activities and complete DGCCRF notification before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Blocked Capital Escrow Account and Issuance of Deposit Attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed French credit institution of the founders' choice, the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or a notary acting as sequester (séquestre).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the company in formation and transfer the cash subscriptions (recommended EUR 1,000, or the amount stated in the Statuts). The depositary issues an attestation de blocage des fonds certifying the amount deposited and its blocked status. The escrow is released automatically upon presentation of the Kbis after RCS registration. The founders must satisfy the depositary's mandatory KYC/AML due diligence.
required_dossiers: Extract of the draft Statuts showing subscribed capital
AML/KYC documentation of each contributing shareholder (identity, source of funds)
Written founders' mandate to open the temporary account
Beneficial-owner declaration for the depositary's files
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the credit institution refuses the file because of the high-risk e-commerce dietary-supplement activity, apply to a specialised acquiring/merchant bank or rely on the statutory alternative of deposit with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations or a notarial séquestre; reinforce the file with a compliance programme and transactional projections.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), acting under the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique. Professional filing portal: impots.gouv.fr (Espace Professionnel). Business and VAT identification is procured through the single-window Guichet Unique des formalités d'entreprises operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr). Customs and export-declaration counterpart: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) via its ATLAS/DELTA electronic clearance platforms. Electronic invoicing infrastructure: Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) with accredited Plateformes de Dématérialisation Partenaires (PDPs).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Route A for a French-established SAS: incorporation is filed electronically via the INPI Guichet Unique; DGFiP automatically issues the SIREN/SIRET and the French intra-Community VAT identification number in the mandatory format FR + two check digits + 9-digit SIREN. No separate VAT-registration application is required at formation; the SAS must confirm activation of the VAT account with its local Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) and file corporate income tax (IS) and VAT returns through impots.gouv.fr. Route B for a non-French remote seller supplying into France: EU-established sellers register directly at the competent SIE using Form 3559-SD without a fiscal representative; non-EU sellers without an EU establishment must file Form 3571-SD and appoint a fiscal representative (représentant fiscal) under CGI Article 289 A, who becomes jointly and severally liable for French VAT unless the seller is established in a treaty country with mutual administrative assistance. For pure B2C distance sales of imported consignments not exceeding EUR 150, the Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) election on the French OSS portal avoids a full VAT registration; intra-EU B2C distance sales are covered by the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) above the EUR 10,000 annual distance-sales threshold. In the nutraceuticals segment, the statutory DGCCRF notification as a 'complément alimentaire' must precede first marketing and is routinely cross-checked by DGFiP auditors against the VAT registration and export records.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a société par actions simplifiée (SAS) is an opaque legal person subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) under CGI Article 206, computed on a territorial-scope basis: profits attributable to French business operations are taxable in France, whereas profits from foreign fixed establishments and foreign real estate are excluded absent an approved worldwide-profits election under CGI Article 209 A. No pass-through or fiscal-transparency election is available for an SAS under French domestic law; the SAS itself is the sole VAT taxable person for all its supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no US-style 'check-the-box' election and offers no elective hybrid-mismatch regime; hybrid and reverse-hybrid outcomes are neutralised automatically by statute under the ATAD/NIEC transposition (loi n° 2019-759). Available elective mechanisms for an SAS: (1) intra-group fiscal integration (CGI Articles 223 A et seq.) at a 95%+ shareholding, permitting group profit pooling, loss transfer and neutrality on intra-group transfers; (2) the small-business reduced corporate rate of 15% on the first EUR 42,500 of annual profit where group turnover is EUR 10 million or less (CGI Article 219 I-b); (3) worldwide/consolidated profits election (CGI Article 209 A) subject to prior ministerial approval; (4) the small-business VAT exemption (franchise en base de TVA, CGI Article 293 B) below the applicable turnover ceilings for goods and services, which forfeits input-VAT deduction and is incompatible with OSS/IOSS participation and export-resale models; (5) OSS/IOSS participation for cross-border B2C distance sales and low-value import consignments; and (6) the single-taxable-person group VAT election (assujetti unique) now transposed into French law, available to qualifying VAT groups.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) as the central bank and monetary authority, together with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance, which exercises foreign-exchange control and foreign-investment screening powers under the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier, CMF), notably Articles L511-1, L151-1 to L152-5 and R152-1 to R153-5.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible, and France maintains no current-account or capital-account exchange restrictions. Capital movements, payments and transfers between France and non-residents are fully liberalised under EU Directive 88/361/EEC, implemented by CMF Articles L221-1 to L221-3. Profit remittance by a French SAS is unrestricted once the annual financial statements have been approved by the shareholders. The practical hurdles for an e-commerce nutraceutical entity are limited to (i) the Banque de France monthly balance-of-payments reporting obligation for cross-border transactions aggregating more than EUR 750,000 in a calendar year; (ii) French withholding tax on dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders, generally 25% for a non-resident company under Article 119-bis of the French General Tax Code (CGI) and 30% global levy for non-resident individuals, reduced or eliminated under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (0%) or an applicable double-tax treaty; and (iii) inbound foreign direct investment screening only where the non-EU investor operates in a defined sensitive sector. Online dietary-supplement retail under ISIC 4791 is not a sensitive sector, so no prior FDI authorisation is required, although a CERFA 16473 declaration may be triggered above threshold levels in certain group structures.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no statutory surrender rule and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. A French exporting SAS may retain, denominate, transfer or convert its export proceeds freely in EUR or foreign currency; there is no repatriation deadline. Two compliance obligations apply: (i) any bank account opened outside France must be declared annually to the French tax administration on Form 3916-bis; and (ii) if the aggregate value of the company's transactions with non-residents exceeds EUR 750,000 per calendar year, the exporter must file a monthly balance-of-payments declaration with the Banque de France via the TéléBOP system, using the non-resident transaction report, which captures export receipts and financial flows. No conversion into euros is required.

Compte de dépôt de capital and compte courant professionnel; cash-pooling host

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability: Medium-High as a complementary rail, Low as a sole treasury rail. ACPR-licensed French payment institutions and electronic-money institutions, including Qonto, Pōs, Treezor (Groupe BPCE) and Vialink, offer remote onboarding, SEPA-instant credit transfers and SWIFT connectivity, and are a legal option for a French SAS. However, standard acceptable-use policies of most EMIs exclude high-risk nutraceutical merchant activation, and EMIs are not a substitute for a high-risk merchant acquirer for card clearing. A non-EEA offshore digital EMI is not compliant as a primary treasury rail because it cannot hold funds in France, cannot provide a French IBAN under the CMF rules applicable to payment services, and creates AML/UBO transparency and substance-evasion risks. Any EMI used must be an EEA-licensed institution passported into France under the CMF pass-porting regime, with a registered branch or appointed agent, and its balances must be consolidated and disclosed in the SAS statutory accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a high-risk, licence-based SAS selling dietary supplements online, enhanced due diligence under CMF Articles L561-5 and R561-5 is mandatory. Purely remote onboarding is legally possible under the CMF implementing provisions where no unusual-risk factors exist, using a qualified electronic signature and an approved video-identity verification solution. In practice, Tier-1 French banks require at least one physical meeting of the legal representative(s) and ultimate beneficial owner(s) at the commercial branch, together with original identity documents, certified statutes, the Kbis extract and a tax-clearance certificate. Remote opening is thus available only in a hybrid form: digital pre-submission of documents followed by mandatory branch interview before issuance of the RIB and activation of the treasury limits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk merchant category classification for online sale of dietary supplements and nutraceuticals (MCC 5122 / 5499), with the absence of a clear French statutory authorisation or licence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: DGCCRF food-supplement pre-marketing declaration file, including the ELIP form and the complete 'déclaration de mise sur le marché' under Article 15 of Directive 2002/46/EC and French Decree 2006-352; SIRENE registration showing the NAF/NACE 4791 activity; Kbis extract and SAS statutes; laboratory certificates of analysis and composition demonstrating compliance with Règlement (UE) 1169/2011; supply-chain traceability records for each imported batch; written designation of the LCB-FT compliance officer; internal risk-rated client acceptance policy and AML procedures manual.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Chargeback and friendly-fraud exposure exceeding bank internal thresholds (typically 1.0% to 1.5% of monthly card volume) combined with e-commerce cross-border card anonymity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six to twelve months of merchant acquiring statements evidencing chargeback ratios, refund policy and service levels; EMV 3-D Secure (3DS2) activation certificate and authentication logs; anti-fraud workflow documentation including AVS, device-fingerprinting and velocity rules; internal AML/CFT procedures; consumer-complaint resolution log; PCI-DSS attestation of compliance for the e-commerce platform and payment page.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque or non-resident UBO chain, particularly a final individual or holding company resident in a low-tax or zero-tax jurisdiction, triggering enhanced source-of-funds and economic-substance review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated French UBO register filing under CMF Article L561-2-2 with the full ownership chain and attestation of absence of nominees; passports and tax-residence certificates for every ultimate beneficial owner; source-of-funds evidence, including shareholder bank statements and SWIFT receipts for prior capital injections; board minutes and shareholders' resolutions evidencing the funding decision; French premises lease, payroll records and corporate-policy documentation demonstrating real economic substance; audited or certified financial statements of the French SAS and, if relevant, group consolidated statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP or negative-media screening hits involving counterparties, shipping routes or payment corridors, or any UBO identified as a politically exposed person.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time screening log against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council sanctions list and French national asset-freeze list; disambiguated name, date-of-birth and country-of-interest data; frozen-asset attestation and confirmation that no transaction is blocked; for PEP exposure, a declaration of political exposure, source-of-wealth file and a lawyer's compliance opinion; denied-party transaction refusal policy; end-use declaration for exported goods confirming consumer nutraceutical use and absence of dual-use or prohibited applications.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for inbound equity injection from a non-resident shareholder: (1) prepare and execute the SAS shareholders' written decision authorising the 'apport en capital' or capital increase; (2) deposit the funds into a 'compte bloque en formation' held in the name of the SAS avec mention 'société en formation' at a Tier-1 French bank, or remit the funds to a notary or to the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations for attestation, before filing the Kbis modification; (3) instruct the paying bank to issue an SWIFT MT103, or an ISO 20022 pacs.008 for EEA-origin transfers, with beneficiary IBAN beginning FR76, beneficiary name FR_SAS, and Field 70 Remittance Information containing purpose code 'EQUI' (equity financing) or 'CAPT' (capital payment) together with the reference 'apport en capital social / prime d'émission, exercice N'; (4) make available to the receiving bank the shareholders' resolution, notarial or bank attestation of capital deposit, Kbis extract and UBO declaration; (5) no prior exchange-control authorisation is required for this non-sensitive sector, but the French company must include the flow in its Banque de France monthly TéléBOP non-resident declaration if aggregate non-resident transactions exceed EUR 750,000 in the calendar year; (6) if the shareholder funds the entity by interest-bearing shareholder loan rather than equity, apply the French thin-capitalisation rules of Article 212-bis CGI, evidence the loan by a written 'convention de compte courant d'associé' at arm's length, and report the credit in the same TéléBOP file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails configured in priority order: (a) SEPA Instant Credit Transfer or SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pacs.008) for all EEA suppliers and service providers, with settlement in euro in one business day or less; (b) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer for non-EEA supplier invoices denominated in USD, GBP, CHF or CNH, using standard ISO 20022 purpose codes such as 'TRAD' for trade transactions and 'PURC' for purchase-payment of goods, with mandatory screening of beneficiary banks against EU, OFAC and UN sanctions lists; (c) an irrevocable documentary letter of credit (Commercial LC, MT700 under ICC Uniform Customs and Practice UCP 600) opened by the French bank in favour of foreign raw-materials manufacturers, with sight or usance tenors of 30 to 90 days and documents comprising commercial invoice, Bill of Lading or temperature-controlled Air Waybill, certificate of analysis and certificate of origin; (d) consumer refunds and chargeback settlements cleared through the high-risk merchant acquiring account via the Visa and Mastercard dispute rails; and (e) intra-group cash-pooling through a zero-balancing SEPA structure supported by a written intercompany financing agreement to avoid recharacterisation as undeclared 'compte courant d'associé'.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD deliverable forward (achat à terme de devises) for USD-denominated ingredient purchases and international marketing costs, tenors typically 1 to 24 months, requiring an underlying commercial exposure and execution under the FBF or ISDA Master Agreement.

Outright EUR/CNH deliverable forward and, where the supplier requires onshore CNY settlement, a non-deliverable forward (NDF) on EUR/CNY executed through a Paris or London dealing desk, so that no onshore CNY account or convertibility approval is needed.
Vanilla European-style EUR/USD and EUR/CNH foreign-exchange options (put/call) with net premium upfront, used to hedge budget rates while preserving upside on uncertain cross-border e-commerce flows.
FX swaps (swap de change) for managing short-term mismatches between incoming USD or CNH receipts and euro operating disbursements, with maturity not exceeding 12 months.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (swap de devises) available only where a long-term supplier financing facility or intercompany loan exists, documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and subject to EMIR trade reporting and clearing-threshold self-assessment, with the SAS qualifying as a non-financial counterparty below the clearing threshold.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS registration confirmation (confirmation d'inscription au RCS; formerly déclaration annuelle de conformité)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises managed by INPI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the anniversary date of the company's registration in the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to respond to the Registrar's annual confirmation request triggers a formal notice; continued non-compliance can lead to administrative removal from the RCS and loss of legal existence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements filing (dépôt des comptes annuels, including bilan, compte de résultat, annexes and management report if required)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés via Guichet Unique (INPI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval within six months after the fiscal year-end; accounts must be filed within one month after approval; for a 31 December year-end the filing is generally required by mid-year unless extended by court order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is subject to criminal fines up to EUR 1,500 for individuals and EUR 7,500 for legal entities; the company may also be prevented from making lawful dividend distributions until filing is completed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership particulars (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs renewal within RCS data confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés via Guichet Unique (INPI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Updated within 30 days after any shareholding or beneficial ownership change; verified in the annual RCS confirmation cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or omitted declaration is punishable by fines up to EUR 7,500 for natural persons and EUR 37,500 for legal entities; repeat violations may trigger criminal liability and strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale n°2065 and related schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December year-end, filing is due by the second working day after 1 May; for other fiscal year-ends, within three months of the closing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 10% late-filing penalty plus monthly late interest of 0.20%; the penalty increases to 40% after formal notice, and criminal tax evasion sanctions may apply.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory when the SAS exceeds at least two of these thresholds: total balance sheet over EUR 4,000,000; annual pre-tax turnover over EUR 8,000,000; average workforce over 50. An auditor may also be required upon shareholder demand, court appointment, or as a condition of group consolidated financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual statutory accounts must be prepared in accordance with French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général issued by the ANC, together with Code de commerce provisions). IFRS may be used only for consolidated accounts of non-listed groups where permitted; the French statutory accounts remain under French GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law does not require a separate standalone annual UBO filing. The beneficial owner declaration is filed at initial RCS registration and must be updated within 30 days after any share transfer or ownership change. The annual RCS confirmation procedure requires the company to verify that the beneficial ownership particulars reflected in the RCS file remain accurate.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (registre des associés and share-transfer movement register for SAS nominative shares)

Register of Directors (French equivalent: President's decisions register and authorized corporate officers' decisions ledger; no separate UK-style register exists, but all corporate governance decisions must be retained at the registered office)
Minute Book (registre des décisions: procès-verbaux of the sole shareholder or general assembly and presidential decisions, held at the registered office)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250–1,200 per year (approximately EUR 230–1,100), depending on professional registered office provider and Paris or regional location
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000–15,000 for a typical small-to-mid-size SAS with cross-border e-commerce; higher where intra-group transactions, complex tax structures or multi-entity consolidation require additional audit work
